items.title: OpenAI ships the Decisions API: a typed, 10x-faster endpoint for yes/no, choice, and score calls
items.summary: New POST /v1/decisions endpoint on gpt-6-luna skips free-text generation entirely — send a predicate, choice, or score question and get a typed answer with probabilities back, not a paragraph to parse. $0.10/M input tokens, no output-token or cache charges. Public beta now.
items.why: Half the LLM calls in a typical agent pipeline — routing, classification, pass/fail gates — don't need a chat response at all, just a fast structured answer, and this is built specifically for that.
items.action: Swap one routing or classification step in an agent pipeline over to POST /v1/decisions and compare latency against your current prompt-and-parse approach.

eval.reason: New endpoint type, model, and pricing model for structured decisions, not a rehash of prior narrow-decision coverage (different vendor, first-party GA push).

items.title: An OpenAI engineer's concrete framework for evaluating multi-agent systems
items.summary: Gary Stafford (Applied AI Engineer, OpenAI) walks through building evals with Promptfoo for multi-agent workflows: capture realistic agent episodes, combine deterministic checks with an LLM judge, test individual agents and the assembled workflow separately, and fix execution defects before trusting any model comparison.
items.why: The comments confirm the real failure mode is broken tool-call handoffs that an LLM judge will happily wave through, not model quality.
items.action: Next time you're comparing models or prompts for a multi-step agent, add one deterministic check on the handoff/coordination layer before trusting an LLM-judge score.

eval.reason: A concrete technical framework with a worked example and open-source harness, not a conceptual teardown post.

items.title: Vela 2.0: open-weight decision models that also point at the exact PII or hallucinated span
items.summary: KR Labs and the vLLM Semantic Router team released Vela 2.0 (0.3B–9B, Apache-2.0): alongside choice/yes-no/score answers it now returns exact text spans for labels named at request time — PII, unsupported RAG claims, prompt-injection attempts — in one forward pass. The 0.3B size runs on a CPU.
items.why: A CPU-sized, open model that flags PII and ungrounded claims in the same call as a routing decision is a real option for a guardrail layer, not just another benchmark post.
items.action: Try the 0.3B Vela 2.0 checkpoint on a PII or hallucinated-span check you currently run as a separate call, and compare against its published CPU numbers.

eval.reason: Genuine open-weight model release with a new span-answer capability and published benchmarks — different vendor and capability from the Decisions API pick.

items.title: Simon Willison shipped a real blog feature by talking to Codex Desktop while cooking dinner
items.summary: He built and shipped a Newsletters index page for his blog entirely by voice, dictating to Codex Desktop instead of typing — real, if small, production work rather than a toy demo.
items.why: This is ordinary use of voice coding on a real feature, not a stunt — the signal that it has crossed from novelty into something you could actually reach for.
items.action: Next time you're away from the keyboard with a small, well-scoped change in mind, try dictating it to a coding agent with voice input instead of waiting until you're back at your desk.

eval.reason: A real, concrete usage example of voice-driven coding shipping real work, not pure discourse.

items.title: Cole Medin: how big companies actually deploy AI agents (not single chat agents)
items.summary: Built in partnership with Oracle, but the lesson generalizes: enterprises aren't shipping one chat agent, they're building multi-agent 'agentic apps' with every LLM call wrapped in a tested workflow, policy-based security, and a human approving anything that matters.
items.why: This is the gap between a weekend agent demo and something an enterprise actually runs — the workflow and approval-gate pattern around the LLM call, not the model, is what's doing the work.
items.action: 12 minutes — watch it as a sanity check against whatever agent architecture you're currently scoping for production.

eval.reason: Covers concrete deployment patterns (multi-agent orchestration, human-in-the-loop) from a real enterprise context, not a reaction or hype video.
